managementSystems.name: Northwind integrated management system
managementSystems.scopeStatement: Baking and packing of biscuits and snacks at the Pune Plant, and sales, purchasing and administration at the Bengaluru Office, for retail and food-service customers in India.
managementSystems.climateChangeRationale: Hotter summers and an irregular monsoon affect wheat supply, cooling loads on the ovens and heat stress on the production floor.

contextItems.text: The line 2 ovens are ageing: they limit output and use more gas per tonne than line 1.
Rising summer temperatures and an irregular monsoon disturb wheat supply and raise cooling loads.
Large retail customers ask for recyclable packaging on every product by 2026.

contextItems.needs: Consistent quality, on-time delivery and allergen labelling that is always right. Contract quality terms become compliance obligations.
Effluent and air emission limits in the consent to operate are met and reported. These are compliance obligations.

contextItems.text: Employees and contract workers at the Pune Plant
contextItems.needs: A safe workplace, and a say in safety decisions through the safety committee.

clauseAssessments.notes: Changes to the system are planned informally at the Bengaluru Office.

clauseAssessments.justification: Northwind bakes to established recipes and customer specifications; it does no product design or development.

documents.retention: Kept for three years in the production office, then shredded.

revisions.changeNote: First issue of the integrated policy.
Adds the commitment to consult workers and to act on climate risks.
Adds the Bengaluru Office to the scope and the new audit programme.
Adds the hold tag for pallets in quarantine.
revisions.sendBackReason: Say who may release a pallet from quarantine.

riskItems.description: All bakery-grade flour comes from one supplier; a failed delivery stops both lines.
Heat waves and a late monsoon cut wheat quality and push up cooling costs.
Rooftop solar at the Pune Plant would cut grid electricity and its cost.

riskItems.impact: Organic load in the effluent sent to the municipal drain.
riskItems.significanceReason: The consent to operate sets effluent limits, so the board treats it as significant.
riskItems.description: Wash water carries fat and dough to the drain.
Rejected packs and offcuts of laminated film go to landfill.

riskItems.assessedWith: Two line 2 oven operators and the shift supervisor.
riskItems.description: Hot trays and oven doors are handled during each tray change.

riskItems.assessedWith: Two members of the sales team.
riskItems.description: Long hours at screens without breaks or adjustable seating.

riskControls.text: Two weeks of flour held as safety stock.
Grease trap and settling tank before the drain.
Guard rails on the line 2 oven doors.
Adjustable chairs and monitor arms at every desk.

objectives.text: Cut grid electricity per tonne of product at the Pune Plant
Bring customer complaints down to five a quarter
Train every line 2 operator in safe oven handling

readings.note: Line 1 heat recovery came on in August.
Four complaints were about loose seals on one carton size.

auditProgrammes.notes: One audit a quarter, so every clause and both units are covered in the year.

internalAudits.summary: Purchasing and production controls work; supplier re-evaluations are sometimes signed late.
internalAudits.title: Q1 internal audit: purchasing and production at the Pune Plant

internalAudits.summary: Aspects and operational controls are in place. Tray changes on line 2 do not follow the hierarchy of controls; water use is not metered by line.
internalAudits.title: Q2 internal audit: environment and health and safety at the Pune Plant
Q3 internal audit: competence and records at the Bengaluru Office

internalAudits.independenceNote: Divya audits the Pune Plant only; her own approvals at the Bengaluru Office are audited by Sameer.
internalAudits.title: Q4 internal audit: performance evaluation and improvement, both units

internalAudits.cancelReason: The cold store was taken out of use before the audit.
internalAudits.title: Special audit of the cold store

auditChecklistItems.question: Are suppliers evaluated and re-evaluated on time?
Are oven settings controlled for each product?
Is nonconforming product held and marked?
Are aspects reviewed after each change?
Were controls chosen by the hierarchy?
Are workplace inspections done and followed up?
Was the last drill evaluated?
auditChecklistItems.notAuditedReason: The drill report was still with the safety committee.

auditChecklistItems.question: Is the training matrix up to date?

certifications.scopeText: Baking and packing of biscuits and snacks at the Pune Plant.

findings.description: Two supplier re-evaluations were signed after their due date.
Line-side boards show the oven settings for each product, so a check takes seconds.
Line 2 tray changes rely on gloves alone; no engineering control was considered.
Metering water by line would show where washing uses the most.
Calibration records for two packing-line scales could not be found.
Complaint data could be trended by product line.
Contract workers were not invited to the last two safety committee meetings.
The list of compliance obligations does not yet name the consent to operate.

nonconformities.containment: Both scales checked against test weights; results since the last record were checked and held.
nonconformities.correction: Both scales calibrated by an accredited laboratory.
nonconformities.rootCause: Calibration was tracked in a personal spreadsheet that was not handed over.
nonconformities.similarOccurrences: Checked every instrument at both units; no other gaps.
nonconformities.riskReview: None needed: calibration is now a recurring activity.
nonconformities.systemChange: Calibration moved into the activity register with reminders.
nonconformities.effectivenessNote: Two quarterly calibrations since were on time with records filed.
nonconformities.description: Calibration records for two packing-line scales could not be found.

nonconformities.containment: Line 2 tray changes stopped until gloves were at every oven.
nonconformities.correction: Gloves put at each oven; the shift briefed the same day.
nonconformities.rootCause: Gloves were kept in a store away from the ovens, and the tray change was rushed at shift end.
nonconformities.similarOccurrences: Line 1 has the same layout; gloves were moved there too.
nonconformities.riskReview: The oven hazard was re-rated after the incident and a guard rail added.
nonconformities.systemChange: Tray changes added to the line 2 work instruction.
nonconformities.description: An oven tray was moved by hand without heat-resistant gloves during a tray change on line 2.

nonconformities.containment: Two people now do each tray change until a control is chosen.
nonconformities.correction: Guard rail on the line 2 oven doors brought forward.
nonconformities.rootCause: The hazard review did not ask which level of the hierarchy each control was at.
nonconformities.similarOccurrences: The same gap may exist for the fryer; it is in the next hazard review.
nonconformities.description: Line 2 tray changes rely on gloves alone; no engineering control was considered.

nonconformities.cancelReason: The time included a planned hold at the assembly point; the evacuation itself took four minutes.
nonconformities.description: The September evacuation drill took nine minutes against a five-minute target.

nonconformities.containment: The contractor supervisor joins the November committee meeting.
nonconformities.correction: Minutes of the last two meetings shared with the contract workers.
nonconformities.rootCause: The committee invitation list was built from the payroll, which leaves out contract workers.
nonconformities.similarOccurrences: The Bengaluru Office has no contract workers; no other list is built this way.
nonconformities.description: Contract workers were not invited to the last two safety committee meetings.
Water from the pantry spread into the corridor; nobody slipped.

nonconformities.containment: The batch was recalled from three distributors and held at the plant.
nonconformities.description: One batch of butter cookies was packed in cartons without the milk allergen warning.

actions.text: Calibrate both scales and file the certificates.
Put a glove station at every oven and check it each shift.
Replace line 2 trays with trays that have insulated handles.
actions.cancelReason: No supplier makes handled trays for these ovens; the guard rail covers the hazard.

actions.text: Retrain line 2 on the tray-change steps, with a sign-off per operator.

actions.resources: Trial batches on line 1; quality lab time.

actions.text: Fit guard rails on the line 2 oven doors.
Make every line 2 tray change a two-person task.
Trial a compostable film for the snack packs.
actions.cancelReason: The trial film failed the seal tests.

actions.text: Install 150 kW of rooftop solar at the Pune Plant.
Retrain the packing line on carton seal checks.
Move to a new carton supplier.
actions.cancelReason: The current supplier fixed the seal width at no cost.

actions.text: Train every line 2 operator in safe oven handling.
Add a reminder a week before each supplier re-evaluation is due.
Fit a water meter on each washing line.
Trend complaints by product line each month.
actions.cancelReason: Covered by the quarterly data analysis activity.

actions.text: Budget for an audit of the second flour supplier.
Add the climate risk to the three-year business plan.
Hire an energy consultant for the Pune Plant.
actions.cancelReason: The solar installer's energy survey covers it.

managementReviews.minutes: The first integrated review. Quality is certified; environment and health and safety are ready for stage 2 once the stage 1 findings are closed.

reviewInputs.notes: First review in the app: no earlier review actions.
Climate added as an external issue; the line 2 ovens are now an internal issue.
Retailers now ask for recyclable packaging; contract workers want a voice in the committee.
Effluent is significant by decision; packaging waste is not significant yet.
Flour supply and oven burns are the significant items; solar is the main opportunity.
Guard rails fitted; a second flour supplier is being qualified.
Survey score steady; complaints rose in the second quarter.
Energy on track, complaints off track, oven training achieved.
Line 1 efficiency up; line 2 limited by the ovens.
One external audit NC closed; the tray-change NC has actions under way.
One lost-time incident in August; investigation done with worker participation.
Effluent within limits every month; electricity per tonne falling.
Half-yearly evaluation done in September; no open legal gaps.
Q1 and Q2 internal audits reported; stage 2 recommended the certificate.
Flour and packaging suppliers rated; one carton supplier on watch.
Committee meets quarterly; contract workers to be invited.
Solar capital approved; a second quality technician needed in 2025.
Policy revision B shared at both units.
Water metering by line; complaint trending by product.

reviewOutputs.decision: The system is suitable and effective for the current scope.
Meter water by line; trend complaints by product.
Add the Bengaluru Office to the manual; invite contract workers to the committee.
Budget for a supplier audit; a second quality technician next year.
Complaints objective kept; seal checks to be audited.
Keep one integrated audit programme and one review.
Climate risk goes into the business plan.
